version.note: The transferred London LP is expressly labelled Original Edition; Decca’s reissue catalogue corroborates Version 1911. The consulted full score represents that orchestration, not the 1947 revision. The exact early printing reproduced by Dover, and any session-specific corrections to players’ parts, remain unidentified.

performers.note: Conductor and ensemble are printed on the sleeve and labels. No individual pianist, celesta player, harpist or other orchestral soloist is identified by the consulted carrier or reissue credits; those names remain unknown.

date.note: Decca discography entry S183[d] specifies 23–25 and 28 October, and 9 November 1957; the displayed value encloses these non-contiguous sessions. The HDTT reissue independently gives the same outer range. The individual tableau's recording day and take dates remain unknown. Release and digitisation dates are not substituted for session dates.

place.note: Decca discography entry S183 and the reissue recording information explicitly name Victoria Hall, Geneva; the venue is not inferred from the orchestra's home city.

label.value: London Records; manufactured by The Decca Record Company Limited, England
label.note: The source is a stereo London LP with red labels; the sleeve is printed in the USA and Archive metadata gives country US. The cover’s ffss designation and the label’s ffrr wording are retained as physical-carrier observations.

Specific equalisation, noise reduction, de-clicking, pitch correction, tape editing and restoration settings remain unknown; Processed by SoX is not evidence of any particular restoration operation.

digital.format: Variable-bit-rate MP3 access derivative of the Internet Archive LP digitisation; track segmentation metadata points back to the digitised side masters. The source filename is preserved verbatim.

composition.value: Underlying 1911 composition and original 1912 score are public domain in the United States; the ordinary EU life-plus-70 composition term has not expired.
composition.note: Stravinsky died in 1971, giving an ordinary EU term through 31 December 2041. This is a territorial term calculation, not worldwide clearance, and it does not grant rights in modern editions, stage designs or choreography. The viewable score is hosted in the US; recording-term eligibility below does not clear the underlying composition.

recording.value: Rule 3 — first lawful publication anywhere before 1963: London CS 6009, commercially published by 1958. Territorial EU sound-recording basis only; US sound-recording status is not established.
recording.note: A contemporary London/Pecar Electronics advertisement in the Grosse Pointe News, 6 November 1958, p. 7, pictures this Petrushka/Ansermet cover with catalogue CS 6009 under recordings NOW AVAILABLE. This directly establishes commercial availability in 1958; Archive's 1958 carrier date and Decca's ℗ 1958 attribution corroborate it. The rule concerns first lawful publication anywhere, not first EU publication; the US advertisement is therefore pertinent. A 1958 lawful publication exhausted the former 50-year EU performance/phonogram term by the end of 2008, before the 1 November 2013 protection threshold for the 70-year extension. The exact earliest market/day and any earlier issue are not established or required for this pre-1963 finding. No CC licence, worldwide public-domain claim, or US recording clearance is asserted.

rights.creditLine: Igor Stravinsky, Petrushka (1911 original orchestration), IV. The Shrovetide Fair (evening); Orchestre de la Suisse Romande, Ernest Ansermet. Recorded 1957, Victoria Hall, Geneva; London CS 6009, 1958. Internet Archive LP digitisation, 29 June 2021. Territorial EU recording-term basis only; US recording status unestablished and composition rights separate.
